# onpager_service_alert_channel (Resource)

Manage one team or service catalog binding to an existing delivery channel and target.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "onpager_service_alert_channel" "example" {
  service_id          = var.service_id
  delivery_channel_id = var.delivery_channel_id
  target_id           = var.target_id
}

variable "service_id" {
  description = "Existing service UUID."
  type        = string
}

variable "delivery_channel_id" {
  description = "Existing delivery-channel UUID; not the catalog binding UUID."
  type        = string
}

variable "target_id" {
  description = "Existing compatible, authorized and enabled target UUID in that channel."
  type        = string
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `delivery_channel_id` (String) Explicit existing delivery-channel UUID. Distinct from the catalog binding's `id`. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.
- `service_id` (String) Owning service UUID. Changing it replaces this resource. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.
- `target_id` (String) Explicit existing delivery-target UUID in the selected channel. No discovery or delivery is performed. Must be a nonzero canonical lowercase UUID.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Stable catalog binding UUID, distinct from the delivery-channel UUID. Import uses owner_uuid/binding_uuid.
- `unavailable` (Boolean) Whether the retained binding's delivery channel or target is currently unavailable.

## Import

Import using `service_uuid/binding_uuid`. The binding UUID differs from the
delivery channel UUID; the API URL's `channel_id` position identifies the
binding.

Use an `import` block:

```terraform
import {
  to = onpager_service_alert_channel.example
  id = "22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222/55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555"
}
```

Or use the CLI:

```shell
terraform import onpager_service_alert_channel.example 22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222/55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555
```

## Lifecycle

This resource owns one explicit catalog binding. The delivery catalog must
already contain a compatible, authorized and enabled channel and target. Use
explicit channel and target UUIDs; name lookup and target discovery are not
supported. Unavailable bindings remain managed.

Changing the delivery channel or target updates the pair in place, preserving
the binding UUID. This update requires both create and delete grants. Create and
update require an active owner. Writes have no revision precondition. Refresh
and import use the exact scoped detail read. Inactive owners do not hide
retained bindings or prevent authorized cleanup.

Destroy deletes only the binding; the delivery channel and target remain.
References can block deletion; remove them explicitly. HTTP failures retain
state. A confirmed `404 not_found` during refresh removes the resource from
state.

## Permissions

Requires `service_channel_catalogs.read`, `service_channel_catalogs.create` and
`service_channel_catalogs.delete` in the owning team, plus access to the
explicit delivery channel and target. Service accounts require explicit native
grants.
